nodes.purpose: Checks a condition at intervals and continues when it becomes true.
nodes.usage: Checks immediately, then at intervals. true fires On Complete; false keeps waiting. Exhausting the check limit uses Timed Out. Retriggering the same node replaces its previous wait.
nodes.example: Integer variable >= 10 → Condition; interval 0.2 seconds. Continue when the variable reaches 10.
nodes.warning: Failure means invalid parameters, such as an interval below 0.1 seconds. A false condition is not failure. Leaving the level or changing stage cancels the wait. Variables and pure calculations are reread, while event objects and loop indices retain their original trigger context.

nodes.purpose: Repeats an action until a condition becomes true, then continues.
nodes.usage: Checks immediately. false runs the loop body, waits the interval and checks again; true fires On Complete. Exhausting the check limit uses Timed Out. Retriggering replaces the previous loop.
nodes.example: Condition: Integer variable >= 10. Each iteration adds 1, with interval 0.2 seconds. Completes at 10. Wait Until only waits; this node also repeats actions.
nodes.warning: Failure means invalid parameters, such as an interval below 0.1 seconds. false runs the loop body. Leaving the level or changing stage cancels the loop. Variables and pure calculations are reread, while event objects and loop indices retain their original trigger context.

nodes.purpose: Fires on a valid left-click on a living zombie on the battlefield.
nodes.usage: Fires on a valid left-click on a living zombie on the battlefield.
nodes.example: Connect Trigger to Damage Zombie and the zombie output to its target for a click-to-defeat mechanic.
nodes.warning: Queries colliders only for valid battlefield clicks. If zombies overlap, selects the nearest to the click. Does not block the original card or tool action.

nodes.purpose: Listens for the global Ice-shroom effect or a row's Jalapeno effect.
nodes.usage: Listens for the global Ice-shroom effect or a row's Jalapeno effect.
nodes.example: Select Jalapeno; the row output identifies the row where fire occurred.
nodes.warning: Ice-shroom affects the whole lawn and returns row -1. Listens to both plant effects and nodes calling the same effect entry point. Avoid feeding this event back into the same effect and causing recursion.

nodes.purpose: Controls whether zombies entering the house trigger the normal loss condition.
nodes.usage: Controls whether zombies entering the house trigger the normal loss condition.
nodes.example: On Level Start → this node, Lose on House Entry=false; determine victory/defeat with events.
nodes.warning: Changes only the house-entry check. Protected-plant death, explicit defeat and other loss conditions remain. With this off, zombies keep walking and leave at the original left boundary under normal rules.

nodes.purpose: Pauses automatic wave advancement while spawned zombies continue acting.
nodes.usage: Pauses automatic wave advancement while spawned zombies continue acting.
nodes.example: Dialogue starts → Paused=true; dialogue finishes → Paused=false.
nodes.warning: Pauses the next-wave timer and early advancement from low remaining enemy HP. Does not interrupt spawning already in progress for this wave. Automatically clears when the event graph stops.

nodes.purpose: Deletes gravestones, craters, ladders or ice blocks in a specified cell.
nodes.usage: Deletes gravestones, craters, ladders or ice blocks in a specified cell.
nodes.example: Select crater, row 2, column 3, to remove that cell's day/night crater.
nodes.warning: Uses each obstacle's Die routine to clear board occupancy too. Ice blocks are cell objects, not a Zomboni's full-row ice trail. Rows and columns start at 0.

nodes.purpose: Plays a selected built-in music track.
nodes.usage: Plays a selected built-in music track.
nodes.example: Stage-entry event → this node; select the stage's background music.
nodes.warning: Uses only loaded game music. On leaving the level, normal menu music handling resumes. Do not call every frame or playback will repeatedly restart.

nodes.purpose: Removes an Odyssey Modifier from this run, stops its ongoing effects and refreshes affinities.
nodes.usage: Select a category and enter an internal name, ID, game display title or full description. A valid but unowned modifier completes normally with Removed=false. Invalid names or ambiguous titles use failure.
nodes.example: Under Zombie Modifiers, the modifier displayed in English as Breakthrough has the internal name 二爷无视植物. Enter that exact internal name; do not assume the translated title is accepted by the game's lookup.
nodes.warning: Unregisters listeners and stops ongoing loops. Strength and the entry internally named 电力相生 clear their separate multipliers; Iron Curtain refreshes from remaining levels. Already granted resources, cards, entities and permanent stat changes are not rolled back. Existing shields and curses end under their own rules. Odyssey entries also remove their secondary records.

nodes.purpose: Recursively breaks down a fusion recipe into its basic plant-type components.
nodes.usage: Recursively breaks down a fusion recipe into its basic plant-type components.
nodes.example: Supply a fusion plant type and iterate the returned types to inspect its components. Repeated ingredients are retained.
nodes.warning: Uses static recipes, not a guess at the actual history of random fusions. A plant with no recipe returns itself. Recipe cycles and excessive recursion depth are guarded.

nodes.purpose: Combines three Float values into world coordinates.
nodes.usage: Combines three Float values into world coordinates.
nodes.example: X=0, Y=1, Z=0 → Create Event Object's position.
nodes.warning: Null objects, type mismatches or out-of-range inputs use failure outputs/default values rather than creating invalid entities.

nodes.purpose: Reads the mouse's world position and cell on the battlefield.
nodes.usage: Reads the mouse's world position and cell on the battlefield.
nodes.example: World position → Create Event Object; row/column → cell-action nodes.
nodes.warning: Outside the board, row/column may be out of bounds. Entity-spawn nodes validate the range.

nodes.purpose: Creates an empty object managed by this event graph, optionally decorated with a plant icon.
nodes.usage: Creates an empty object managed by this event graph, optionally decorated with a plant icon.
nodes.example: Choose Peashooter as the icon and create a decorative marker at the mouse position.
nodes.warning: A visual marker, not an attacking plant or occupied cell. Maximum 256 living objects per graph, cleaned up when it ends. Use dedicated spawn nodes for real plants/zombies.

nodes.purpose: Stores an object under a name for later events to retrieve.
nodes.usage: Stores an object under a name for later events to retrieve.
nodes.example: Bind as "Marker1", then use String to Object with "Marker1" later.
nodes.warning: The same name replaces the previous binding. Names are local to the running graph. Pooled projectiles require dedicated handles, not long-lived scene-object references.

nodes.purpose: Generates reference text unique to the object in the current running graph.
nodes.usage: Generates reference text unique to the object in the current running graph.
nodes.example: Store object-reference text in a String list, then retrieve it through String to Object.
nodes.warning: A token for this run, not an object name or a save ID usable across levels. Null objects, pooled projectiles or exceeding 1024 simultaneous valid references return an empty string.

nodes.purpose: Resolves object-reference text or an object binding name.
nodes.usage: Resolves object-reference text or an object binding name.
nodes.example: Enter "Marker1" to retrieve the marker saved by Bind Object.
nodes.warning: Invalid, destroyed or different-run references return null. Does not scan the whole scene by name or create an object.

nodes.purpose: Converts a plant to a scene-object reference.
nodes.usage: Converts a plant to a scene-object reference.
nodes.example: Use for object bindings, Object lists or reading position.
nodes.warning: Null objects, type mismatches or out-of-range inputs use failure outputs/default values rather than creating invalid entities.

nodes.purpose: Reads a plant component from an object.
nodes.usage: Reads a plant component from an object.
nodes.example: Get an item from an Object list, convert to Plant, then use existing combat nodes.
nodes.warning: Null objects, type mismatches or out-of-range inputs use failure outputs/default values rather than creating invalid entities.

nodes.purpose: Converts a zombie to a scene-object reference.
nodes.usage: Converts a zombie to a scene-object reference.
nodes.example: Use for object bindings, Object lists or reading position.
nodes.warning: Null objects, type mismatches or out-of-range inputs use failure outputs/default values rather than creating invalid entities.

nodes.purpose: Reads a zombie component from an object.
nodes.usage: Reads a zombie component from an object.
nodes.example: Get an item from an Object list, convert to Zombie, then use existing combat nodes.
nodes.warning: Null objects, type mismatches or out-of-range inputs use failure outputs/default values rather than creating invalid entities.

nodes.purpose: Reads an object's world position, scale and existence.
nodes.usage: Reads an object's world position, scale and existence.
nodes.example: Convert a plant to an object and read its position to place a decorative object there.
nodes.warning: Null objects, type mismatches or out-of-range inputs use failure outputs/default values rather than creating invalid entities.

nodes.purpose: Moves and scales markers made by Create Event Object.
nodes.usage: Moves and scales markers made by Create Event Object.
nodes.example: Move a marker to the mouse position with scale 0.5.
nodes.warning: Changes only decorative objects created by the event graph. Use dedicated movement nodes for plants/zombies; changing only their Transform can break cell occupancy or row indexing.

nodes.purpose: Deletes a scene marker created by the current event graph.
nodes.usage: Deletes a scene marker created by the current event graph.
nodes.example: Delete a bound temporary marker.
nodes.warning: Can delete only objects owned by this graph. Use dedicated nodes for plants, zombies, cards and other entities to preserve game cleanup behavior.

nodes.purpose: Selects a built-in projectile type.
nodes.usage: Selects a built-in projectile type.
nodes.example: Bullet_pea is a normal pea. Both sides can fire the same projectile type.
nodes.warning: Firing fails if the type's resource is not loaded. Movement uses straight-line flight at the specified angle.

nodes.purpose: Fires a projectile from a specified cell or mouse position in a chosen direction.
nodes.usage: Fires a projectile from a specified cell or mouse position in a chosen direction.
nodes.example: Row 2, column 3.5, damage 20, speed 6, angle 0, size 1. Angle 180 points left.
nodes.warning: Rows/columns start at 0. Angles: 0 right, 90 up, 180 left, 270 down. Uses the game's object pool and collision effects. Out-of-bounds projectiles or those older than 20 seconds are recycled under game rules.

nodes.purpose: Changes a still-active event projectile's size, speed, damage or direction.
nodes.usage: Changes a still-active event projectile's size, speed, damage or direction.
nodes.example: Choose direction angle and value 90 to turn the projectile upward.
nodes.warning: A recycled projectile uses failure, even if its GameObject has been reused for a new projectile. Size is relative to this projectile's original size; repeated settings do not compound.

nodes.purpose: Switches day/night backgrounds within a terrain group, preserving entities and ice trails.
nodes.usage: Switches day/night backgrounds within a terrain group, preserving entities and ice trails.
nodes.example: On a Day map, connect a stage event and select Night to switch to night.
nodes.warning: Supported groups: Day/Night, Day_6/Night_6, Pool/NightPool, Roof/NightRoof, the three Odyssey roof variants, the three Mesa River variants, and SnowPool day/night variants. Other groups or special maps use failure and leave the board unchanged. Minimum 1 second between changes. Sun, cells, entities, waves and game speed are unchanged. Literal map IDs are not translated.

nodes.purpose: Processes every living zombie currently on the battlefield.
nodes.usage: Processes every living zombie currently on the battlefield.
nodes.example: Each iteration → Set Zombie Status; current zombie → target.
nodes.warning: Takes one snapshot when triggered. Newly spawned zombies join only the next snapshot; zombies that die during iteration are skipped. Includes hypnotized zombies, so filter if needed.

nodes.purpose: Sets a plant's own base attack interval.
nodes.usage: Sets a plant's own base attack interval.
nodes.example: Enter 0.5 seconds to make that plant's base wait between attacks 0.5 seconds.
nodes.warning: Range 0.05 to 3600 seconds. Attack-speed bonuses still follow the original formula. Affects only plants using the base attack interval; does not reset current attack animations or special-ability timers.

nodes.purpose: Runs the actual Golden Coffee Bean feeding process on a plant.
nodes.usage: Runs the actual Golden Coffee Bean feeding process on a plant.
nodes.example: Connect Trigger and the plant target to attempt feeding automatically. Check Applied to see whether feeding succeeded.
nodes.warning: The player need not pick up a bean. Normal coin costs, upgrade eligibility and Ultimate conditions still apply and the usual cost is charged. On Complete means the attempt finished; Applied means it succeeded. The separate Try Plant Ultimate node calls the ability for free but skips Silver-plant upgrades and feeding-related effects.

nodes.purpose: Refers to a shared String variable.
nodes.usage: Press + String in Level Variables, set its initial value, drag it onto the canvas, and connect a String getter or setter.
nodes.example: Set a String variable to "Objective complete" → Show Text.
nodes.warning: Copied references share the same variable; template variables are copied independently.

nodes.purpose: Refers to a shared typed list.
nodes.usage: Press + List in Level Variables, select an element type and enter initial values, then drag it onto the canvas.
nodes.example: Integer list → List Length; trigger Append Integer, then read the length again.
nodes.warning: Indices start at 0; maximum 512 items. Element types must match operation nodes. Copying a list copies values into a separate container. Object initial values are object binding names.
